text:
Priya Shah: Heads up — seeing sustained pod evictions in ap-southeast1 (~03:10-04:00 UTC). Mostly tiny-gang jobs and a few dedicated slots. Nodes report "egress: connection reset" in kube-proxy logs.
Alex Gomez: Which pool/zone?
Priya Shah: warm-pool-apse1b and a couple on warm-pool-apse1a. Evictions spike right after autoscaler bursts.
Marco Li: Would guess cross-az egressthrottle — we've hit underlay bandwidth caps a few times when we burst to replace preempted spot racks.
Sasha Ivanov: Seen this before — scheduler packs into apse1b because of affinity labels. When egress saturates, kubelet OOMs and we start soft evicts. :frowning:  
Liam O'Connor: Can we confirm it's egress and not conntrack? Any conntrack exhaustion traces?
Priya Shah: Quick grep from node: ``conntrack: table full`` on 3 nodes, plus dmesg shows TCP resets. So both. Saturated NIC + conntrack holes.
Alex Gomez: Ok — that explains fragmentation: scheduler avoids thinned racks, backfills others, then evict loops. We should throttle autoscaler bursts to avoid spiking egress per-AZ.
infra-bot: autoscaler-event: 2026-03-21T03:12:40Z -> scale up 18 GPUs in ap-southeast1 triggered by queue depth.
Marco Li: Short term: 1) Reduce scale-up step for ap-southeast1 to 4-6 nodes, 2) enable conntrack reclaim on nodes, 3) soft-preempt policy to prefer draining warm pools first.
Sasha Ivanov: Also propose scheduler tweak: avoid scheduling gang jobs cross-azole when egress > 70%. Add a placement weight to prefer AZ spread when network metric high.
Liam O'Connor: Cost callout — reducing burst size will increase queued latency but reduce eviction churn and repeat re-schedules (which cost us wasted GPU minutes). Net expected savings ~12% on that region for the incident window.
Priya Shah: Rolling mitigation applied: patched cluster-autoscaler config to max-burst=6 for apse1, enabled conntrack-gc tweaks (``sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=120``) on the warm-pool AMI, and added a temporary scheduler predicate that prefers nodes with free conntrack headroom.
Alex Gomez: Can you paste the patch snippet?
Priya Shah: ``
# cluster-autoscaler config snippet
scaleDown: true
maxSurge: 6
nodeGroups:
  - name: warm-pool-apse1
    maxSize: 80
    minSize: 6
    maxBurst: 6
``

Priya Shah: And the scheduler predicate is a lightweight plugin that reads node annotation `net/conntrack-headroom` and penalizes nodes with <1000 available entries. It's deployed as a feature flag (off by default).
Marco Li: Long term: we should 1) instrument per-AZ egress throttling for the scheduler, 2) make conntrack reclaim aggressive on GPU AMIs, 3) consider dedicated egress bandwidth reservations for warm-pools during scale events.
Sasha Ivanov: Agreed. I'll sketch an RFC for egress-aware placement and a cost model for reserved egress.
ops-bot: incident-note created: INC-2026-1423 "apse1 eviction storm — egress+conntrack" assigned to eng-infra.
Priya Shah: Post-mortem TODOs: add runbook steps to cap scale-up, add alarm on conntrack usage >75%, and adapt warm-pool sizing in billing forecast.
Liam O'Connor: I'll put the cost calc in the finance channel and estimate committed warm-pool reservation tradeoffs.
Alex Gomez: Thanks team. If evictions resurge after the fixes, escalate to cross-region fallback: route new requests to eu-west1 with lower concurrency rather than force local burst.
Priya Shah: Noted — enabling cross-region fallback in routing policy as a canary. Will follow up with PR. :thumbsup:
